Hi Michael — appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers up front: 1) Capacity swap ops: we have an orchestrated swap process that can reassign reserved SKUs across tiers (e.g., A100 -> A10-equivalent quantized SKUs) in a rolling 72-hour window for up to 20% of committed capacity without contract amendment; swaps beyond that require 10 business day notice and approval. 2) Pricing escalation: we include a GPU-price-trigger clause tied to a published index (monthly average spot price). If the index moves >15% vs. baseline for 30 consecutive days, both parties can reopen the unit price with a 30-day negotiation window and an optional interim floor/ceiling protection.

I'll attach a one-page playbook and the swap runbook showing timeline, rollback steps, and logging we provide to customers. Karthik — can you flag the typical discount approval path (sales + finance thresholds) for Michael so he knows the SLA for approvals? Laura — looped for finance comment on the 15% trigger and whether we can shorten notice for enterprise deals.

Michael — quick note on approvals from the commercial side. For deals in the size band of ORCH-4721 we have a two-tier approval flow: discounts <10% can be signed off by Sales + RevOps (24-48h), discounts 10–25% require Finance (Laura) + Sales leader sign-off (3–5 business days). Anything >25% is an Executive exception and needs a documented business case. For price-trigger reopeners tied to the GPU index, we typically provision a temporary credit/escrow to smooth the transition while Finance reviews — that usually buys 30 days. If you prefer a hard floor/ceiling instead of a negotiation window, we can propose language, but that moves pricing risk to Redwood and will affect discount bands.

If Orchard needs faster cadence for approvals (e.g., 48h on a trigger) we can discuss an accelerated path for an additional contract fee.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales

Looping Finance detail. The 15% index trigger is reasonable as a negotiation threshold, but for ORCH-4721 (expected commit > $1.2M ARR) finance recommends: 1) move trigger to 12% to reduce false positives, 2) include a two-tier mitigation: a short-term credit equal to the difference for up to 60 days while we operationalize a SKU swap, and 3) explicit cap on total credit exposure (we propose a 6% of annual committed spend cap).

If Orchard agrees to accept a 60-day operational window and the proposed exposure cap, we can pre-authorize an accelerated approval runway (48–72 hours) for any rediscount up to 18% without exec sign-off. That provides the faster remediation Orchard requested while limiting financial risk to Redwood.

Neha — confirm we can express the cap and expedited approval in SOW language (I can draft). Michael — if that sounds acceptable I will prepare the specific clause and the numeric example.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance — Commercial Deals
